findings.explanation: aws_cloudtrail.account sets sns_topic_name = aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail.name, but the module creates no aws_sns_topic_policy. AWS requires the target topic's policy to allow cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to sns:Publish; CreateTrail rejects the trail with InsufficientSnsTopicPolicyException otherwise. The default policy created with an aws_sns_topic permits only the owning account, not the service principal. CI runs plan only, so this has never surfaced.
findings.fix: resource "aws_sns_topic_policy" "cloudtrail" { arn = aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail.arn; policy = <cloudtrail publish policy> }
findings.remediation: Add an aws_sns_topic_policy granting sns:Publish to cloudtrail.amazonaws.com, scoped by aws:SourceArn to this trail.
findings.title: SNS topic wired to CloudTrail has no topic policy granting the service publish rights

findings.explanation: target_bucket resolves to s3accesslogging-<account_id> from local.logging. Nothing in this module creates that bucket and no variable lets a consumer point elsewhere. Any consumer without a bucket of exactly that name gets a failed apply partway through, after the trail bucket already exists.
findings.remediation: Expose target_bucket as a variable defaulting to the current local so consumers can point at their own logging bucket, or create the bucket in-module behind a feature flag.
findings.title: S3 access logging targets a bucket the module neither creates nor validates

findings.explanation: var.expiry defaults to 30, so aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration.trails deletes trail objects after 30 days, while var.retention_in_days keeps the CloudWatch copy for 365. S3 is the authoritative long-term store and the only one the Glue/Athena table can query, so the module silently caps historical audit queries at 30 days while implying a year of retention.
findings.remediation: Raise the var.expiry default to match retention_in_days (365), or document the split deliberately.
findings.title: Durable S3 copy of the audit trail expires 12x sooner than the CloudWatch copy

findings.explanation: object_lock_enabled = true only permits per-object locks; with no aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration there is no default retention, so no object is actually immutable and the flag delivers nothing beyond the bucket-replacement cost of enabling it. Conversely, if a default retention rule is added later it will conflict with the 30-day expiration rule, which will begin silently failing to delete locked objects.
findings.remediation: Either add an aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration with a default retention shorter than var.expiry, or drop object_lock_enabled if immutability is not actually wanted.
findings.title: Object Lock enabled on the bucket but never configured, and it conflicts with the lifecycle expiry

findings.explanation: aws_kms_alias.trails.name is the literal alias/cloudtrail, aws_glue_catalog_database.cloudtrail.name is the literal cloudtrail, and local.trails_bucket derives solely from account ID. All three are account- or account-plus-region-unique. A consumer wanting a second trail (a common pattern: one organisation trail plus one account trail) hits AlreadyExists on all three with no variable to work around it. Only log_group_name and trail.name are parameterised.
findings.remediation: Derive all three from var.trail["name"] or add a name_prefix variable.
findings.title: Hardcoded global names prevent the module being instantiated twice in one account

findings.explanation: The table points at the whole s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/AWSLogs/<account>/CloudTrail prefix with no partition_keys, so every Athena query scans every object beneath it. CloudTrail writes a region/year/month/day hierarchy that is the standard partitioning scheme; without it Athena is billed for a full-prefix scan on every query.
findings.remediation: Add partition_keys for region, year, month and day, and either register partitions or switch the table to partition projection via the projection.* table parameters.
findings.title: Glue catalog table declares no partition keys

findings.explanation: No resource in the module sets tags and there is no tags variable. Consumers can only tag via provider default_tags, which the example relies on. That works for blanket tags but leaves no way to tag these resources specifically: cost allocation per trail, ownership, or data classification on the trail bucket.
findings.remediation: Add a tags variable of type map(string) defaulting to {} and merge it into the taggable resources: aws_cloudtrail, aws_s3_bucket, aws_kms_key, aws_sns_topic, aws_cloudwatch_log_group and aws_iam_role.
findings.title: Module exposes no tagging interface

findings.explanation: terraform validate warns on both. data.aws_region.current.name is deprecated in favour of .region and is used in four interpolations across the IAM role policy and the KMS key policy. data.aws_cloudtrail_service_account is deprecated outright in favour of the cloudtrail.amazonaws.com service principal; it is only consumed by the service_account output, so removing it is a breaking output change.
findings.remediation: Replace data.aws_region.current.name with data.aws_region.current.region. Plan removal of the service_account data source and output for the next major version.
findings.title: Two deprecated provider constructs still in use

findings.explanation: transient_lastDdlTime is hardcoded to 1595852255 (2020-07-27), a value copied from whatever console export this table came from. It is a Hive bookkeeping field that means nothing pinned to a fixed date, and it misleads anyone reading the table definition into thinking it records something real.
findings.fix: remove the "transient_lastDdlTime" entry from the parameters map
findings.remediation: Remove the transient_lastDdlTime parameter; Glue populates it itself.
findings.title: Magic epoch timestamp copied into Glue table parameters

suggested_policies.rationale: A trail that names an SNS topic whose topic has no aws_sns_topic_policy is a guaranteed apply failure (InsufficientSnsTopicPolicyException), not a style issue. It is a companion-resource check of exactly the same shape as the existing HLD_AWS_131/144/145 S3 checks, so the engine can decide it deterministically.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_AWS_314
name: SNS topics used by CloudTrail must have a topic policy
principle: reliability
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  aws_cloudtrail.sns_topic_name requires the target topic's access policy to
  grant sns:Publish to cloudtrail.amazonaws.com. The default policy created
  with an aws_sns_topic grants only the owning account, so CreateTrail fails
  with InsufficientSnsTopicPolicyException.
remediation: |
  Add an aws_sns_topic_policy for the topic granting sns:Publish to the
  cloudtrail.amazonaws.com service principal, scoped by aws:SourceArn.
resources:
  aws_sns_topic:
    companion:
      type: aws_sns_topic_policy
      references_via: arn

suggested_policies.rationale: object_lock_enabled = true without an aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration gives no immutability at all while permanently costing a bucket replacement to enable. Unambiguous companion-resource condition, and HLD_AWS_310 already pushes users into exactly the half-configured state this would catch.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_AWS_313
name: Object Lock enabled buckets must have an object lock configuration
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  object_lock_enabled only permits per-object locks. Without an
  aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration setting a default retention rule,
  no object is retained and the flag delivers nothing, having already cost a
  bucket replacement to turn on.
remediation: |
  Add an aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration with a default_retention
  rule, or remove object_lock_enabled.
resources:
  aws_s3_bucket:
    when:
      path: object_lock_enabled
      equals: true
    companion:
      type: aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration
      references_via: bucket
